subject: Request: progressive hedging policy for A/B rollout to meet SLA commitments
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aetherhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: AetherHealth Procurement <procurement@aetherhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: progressive hedging policy to align rollout with uptime SLA

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The platform looked promising. Before we proceed to a pilot, our legal/procurement team asked whether Redwood can formally allow a "progressive hedging" deployment approach for our production cutover.

Context: AetherHealth needs a 99.95% monthly uptime SLA for our patient-facing APIs. Our internal risk team wants a policy that allows A/B or canary rollouts with an automatic revert/pin to a previously verified model variant if latency or error rates cross thresholds that would jeopardize the SLA.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood commit to automatic fallback to the prior pinned version when tail-latency > 95th pct threshold (we propose 350ms P95 over a 5m window) or error rate > 0.5%?
- Will that automatic fallback be considered an acceptable mitigation such that AetherHealth can still sign for 99.95% SLA?
- What telemetry and audit evidence can Redwood provide (logs, trace slices, minutes of cross-region failover) to satisfy our procurement team?

I've attached our draft SLA matrix for reference (aether_sla_matrix.xlsx). Procurement suggested we put this in writing to avoid later surprises. 

Would appreciate a short note from you outlining Redwood's policy + what exceptions we need to formalize in the contract. We're on a tight timeline for May rollouts.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships
AetherHealth

[attachment: aether_sla_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aetherhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: progressive hedging policy to align rollout with uptime SLA

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the detailed note and the SLA matrix. Short answer: yes, we support progressive/A-B rollouts with automatic fallback and version pinning as part of an SLA mitigation strategy. I want to be explicit about how that maps to contractual terms and telemetry so your procurement team can sign off.

High-level approach we propose:
- Canary/A-B with built-in health policies: automatic fallback to last-healthy pinned variant when configured thresholds are breached (latency, error-rate, model confidence for classification tasks).
- Policy enforcement: fallback is executed by the control plane; we record an immutable event (fallback timestamp, reason, metrics snapshot).
- SLA carveout: if a fallback is triggered and Redwood executes within the configured SLO window (we'll propose 90s detection + 60s failover), that incident is treated as mitigated and will not count toward SLA downtime for contract enforcement; if fallback fails or fatal infra issues occur, normal SLA incident rules apply.

I added Karthik and Laura to scope the technical thresholds and legal framing. Next steps: Karthik will propose safe default thresholds and failover timings; Laura can advise on how to phrase the contractual carveout language and what approvals we need internally.

I can draft a short "operation & carveout" clause for your contract once we have the thresholds.

Thanks — will be quick on this.

—Vanessa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Elena / Vanessa —

Quick technical notes from infra/serving side. We're comfortable with the fallback semantics described, but want to set expectations on these points so the contract reflects operational reality:

1) Detection windows and noise: Using a 5-minute sliding window for P95 latency is reasonable, but we recommend a hysteresis buffer to avoid flip-flopping — e.g., require threshold breach for 2 consecutive 1-minute buckets before triggering.
2) Failover timing: 90s detection + 60s failover is aggressive but achievable for single-region setups with warmed pools and KV cache compatibility. Cross-region failover will add propagation time — call that +200–400ms to tail latency during migration.
3) Pinning: Pinning a version prevents automatic updates but does not freeze telemetry collection. When pinned, we will continue to route traffic to the pinned variant until unpinned by the customer or by an authorized Redwood ops playbook in emergency.
4) Evidence/audit: We can provide a zipped incident artifact per fallback (JSON events, sampled traces, P95 slices pre/post) and bucket-level cost/usage delta for the incident. We retain these artifacts for 90 days by default (extendable for enterprise contracts).

Open items for procurement: acceptable numeric thresholds (latency P95 threshold, error-rate threshold) and whether the carveout should apply per-incident or on a rolling monthly budget.

I'll propose defaults: P95 threshold = 350ms, error-rate = 0.5% (per Elena's note), 2-minute confirmation, 90s detection + 60s failover. If AetherHealth prefers stricter numbers, we can discuss trade-offs (more pre-warming, reserved capacity).

Karthik
Head of Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: FWD: Request: progressive hedging policy to align rollout with uptime SLA — approval request

Hi Laura / Aditya —

Forwarding an external request from AetherHealth (Elena) and our proposed mitigation language from Karthik. They want to treat automatic fallback/pinning as an SLA mitigation so they can sign 99.95% uptime.

Key ask for approval:
- Approve the carveout language that treats an automated fallback (with detection+failover within our operational windows) as a mitigated incident and not counted against SLA uptime.
- Confirm default operational windows: P95 threshold 350ms, error-rate 0.5%, 2 consecutive 1-minute confirmation, detection 90s, failover 60s.
- Approve retention of incident artifacts for 90 days and production of an incident ZIP on fallback.

We should also lock whether this carveout is per-incident or part of a monthly "hedge" budget. My recommendation: per-incident carveout up to 3 incidents/month; beyond that SLA applies normally. This protects Redwood from sustained regressions while still giving customers operational flexibility.

Can we get signoff by COB tomorrow? Procurement is hoping to close the pilot contract by Friday.

Thanks —
Vanessa

Vanessa —

I reviewed the proposed operational windows and carveout. Approve with one edit: make the monthly allowance explicit and limit the per-incident carveout to 3 incidents per calendar month per account (as you suggested). If the customer consistently hits the limit we will trigger an operational review and reserve the right to require reserved capacity (Dedicated) or tighter thresholds.

I'll work with Legal to add the following clause to the contract draft: 
"Automatic fallback events executed by Redwood within the agreed detection and failover windows (90s detection, 60s failover) will be treated as mitigated incidents and excluded from SLA downtime calculations, subject to a monthly allowance of up to three (3) mitigated fallback events. Persistent failures beyond this allowance will be subject to standard SLA incident rules and may prompt recommended configuration changes or capacity commitments."

Please proceed to send Elena the confirmation and attach the incident evidence/retention note.

—Laura
